text:
Alex R: Heads-up — HashBridge POC kicks off Monday. We need a short runnable checklist: adapter compatibility tests, pricing Qs for their committed throughput, and security questionnaire answers. Can we sync?
Maria T: I can own adapter tests. Can someone share a sample HashBridge request shape?
Devin L: They use a very tiny wrapper around OpenAPI-style endpoints. Example payload: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "<user prompt>",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stream": false
}
```
We should validate: headers, streaming differences, and role/chat framing.
Samir P: On parity: their default sampling settings differ (top_p 0.95, temp 0.7). We should run a prompt suite and measure response deltas. I'll spin up a small harness.
Jen K: Pricing question from sales: they expect per-request parity with their current vendor. Do we have a mapping doc from HashBridge units to our token-based billing?
Devin L: Quick answer: no 1:1 mapping. Suggest we present an estimate: convert avg response length -> tokens, include inference overhead. I'll draft a sample calc.
Maria T: For adapter tests I need the HashBridge example responses (headers + error codes). Any known weirdness?
Alex R: Their error codes sometimes return 200 with a body {error: "partial"} on partial responses (ugh). We should test for both body-level errors and HTTP errors.
Samir P: Also watch prompt framing — HB prepends a system line and uses different role names (assistant vs bot). We'll need normalization layer. Suggest simple shim: strip/translate roles before diffing.
Jen K: Sales also flagged enterprise blockers: SSO, SCIM provisioning, KMS for customer keys, and SOC2 evidence. Can security confirm which we can commit to?
ComplianceBot: Automated note: Uploaded SBOM and SOC2 summary to the prospect folder: https://redwood.internal/prospects/hashbridge/pocs. Please attach any additional docs.
Maria T: For security questionnaire (they sent 28Q) I can start with the common answers. Jen — can you forward their specific KMS questions?
Jen K: Forwarded. Short answer: we have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), HSM available for Private deployments; Dedicated can support customer-managed keys. Will confirm exact SLA language.
Devin L: For the POC harness, I propose 3 buckets: 1) parity prompts (50 prompts across categories), 2) error/edgecases (10 failure modes), 3) perf/latency (1000 reqs at their expected qps). Anyone opposed?
Alex R: Sounds good. Maria + Samir pair on 1 and 2, Devin on 3. Action items:
- Maria: run adapter tests and collect sample requests/responses.
- Samir: set up parity diff harness, include temperature/top_p adjustments.
- Devin: produce pricing estimate template and perf script.
- Jen: consolidate security answers and KMS wording.
- Alex: coordinate demo and customer-facing notes.
Maria T: I'll push a minimal adapter repo under my fork by EOD Fri and share curl snippets.
Samir P: I'll put together a quick evaluation metric: semantic similarity (embedding cosine), exact-match for structured fields, and a manual spot-check sample.
Devin L: Perf script will be k6-based, example: 
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hashbridge-proxy', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'test'}));
}
```
Jen K: Noted. I'll also ask legal to pre-sign our standard POC NDA; that was a blocker last time.
Alex R: Great. If anything blocks, @jenk and @devin — escalate. We'll do a 30m sync Friday morning.
Jen K: +1 :thumbsup:
Devin L: +1
Maria T: Thanks all — will upload initial samples later today.
Alex R: Closing loop: let's ensure we log response deltas and keep a short FAQ for Sales on expected behavior differences (stream vs chunking, role names, error formats).
